page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-48 is an accelerator-optimized virtual machine featuring four NVIDIA L4 GPUs with 96 GB of aggregated GDDR6 VRAM. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz, configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs (24 physical cores with hyperthreading) and 38 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is 192 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 4 GB per vCPU allocation. Local disk storage is not bundled with this configuration, requiring remote block storage.

In benchmark testing, the system exhibits top-tier performance in AI acceleration, delivering prompt processing speeds of 2720.46 tokens per second on 7B parameter models and 255.89 tokens per second on 70B parameter models. Multi-core compute and memory bandwidth reach average tier thresholds, marked by a multi-core Geekbench score of 10460.0 and uncached memory read bandwidth of 104.62 GB/s. However, single-core processing demonstrates lower efficiency, scoring in the bottom quartile across Geekbench and compression tasks due to the modest 2.2 GHz clock rate.

Hardware resource distribution delivers dense parallel acceleration across four Ada Lovelace GPUs, making it cost-effective for multi-stream AI inference, graphics virtualization, and video transcode pipelines. The primary tradeoff lies between the high GPU capacity and moderate single-thread host CPU performance, alongside the absence of local NVMe storage. Consequently, the instance is optimal for distributed machine learning inference, real-time rendering, and GPU-accelerated ETL, rather than single-threaded CPU-bound or storage-intensive workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-48 is an accelerator-oriented virtual machine featuring four NVIDIA L4 Ada Lovelace GPUs with a combined 96 GB of VRAM, paired with 48 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs and 192 GB of system memory. Operating on the x86_64 architecture at 2.2 GHz, the instance delivers balanced host resources at 4 GB of RAM per vCPU, though it includes no bundled local storage. Benchmark results highlight top-tier capabilities in large language model inference, achieving strong prompt evaluation rates across 7B and 70B parameter models. Conversely, single-thread CPU benchmarks perform in the lower quartile, reflecting modest base clock frequencies, while multi-core compute and memory bandwidth remain in the middle range. Given its dense GPU configuration and moderate host processing power, g2-standard-48 represents an efficient infrastructure choice for high-concurrency machine learning inference, batch video processing, and graphics virtualization workloads that rely on scalable parallel acceleration rather than intense single-core throughput.
